issues.title: [Performance] Add QK RMSNorm+RoPE fusion patch for Step3p5Attention
issues.body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Add a monkey-patch for `Step3p5Attention` that fuses QK GemmaRMSNorm + RoPE into a single `torch.ops.vllm.qkv_rmsnorm_rope` kernel on NPU devices. The step3p5 model applies per-head RMSNorm to Q and K followed by rotary position embedding. On NPU, these three steps (RMSNorm, RoPE on Q, RoPE on K) can be fused into a single Triton kernel along with the QKV split, reducing kernel launch overhead and improving throughput. The model code (`step3p5.py`) remains clean with no NPU-specific logic — all optimization lives in the vllm-ascend patch system, registered alongside other model-specific patches. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. The optimization is transparent to users. The patched forward maintains identical numerical behavior to the original separate QK RMSNorm + RoPE path. ### How was this patch tested? Tested on 8-NPU node with step3p5-flash model (bfloat16, w8a8 quantization, TP=8): vllm serve /path/to/step3p5_flash_weight --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enforce-eager --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-expert-parallel --async-scheduling --speculative_config '{"method":"step3p5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"enable_multi_layers_mtp":true}' - Verified model loads and serves correctly with the patched forward. - Manually compared Q/K/V outputs from fused kernel vs. original split-path on same inputs, results match within bfloat16 tolerance. - The evalscope accuracy test result is as follows: - vLLM version: v0.23.0 - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/a30addc7548a9a8b9b3323a7bc3eb7d7c4895d1c

issues.title: [Ops][Misc] Optimize split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope op
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR optimizes the `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope` operator by introducing a new Triton kernel, `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope_prefill_kernel`, for the prefill stage (i.e., large batch sizes). The implementation now dynamically selects between the existing decode kernel and the new prefill kernel based on the batch size, which improves performance for large batch scenarios.

Additionally, the RoPE implementation is updated to support partial rotation dimensions (`rope_dim`), making the operator more flexible.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is a performance optimization and is not expected to introduce any user-facing changes.

### How was this patch tested?

CI should pass with existing tests. The new prefill path is triggered when the batch size is larger than the number of available vector cores. The partial RoPE feature can be tested by passing the `rope_dim` argument.
- vLLM version: v0.15.0
- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/83b47f67b1dfad505606070ae4d9f83e50ad4ebd
